entries.body: The fictional GitHub organization aldercreek-advisory is on the GitHub Team plan, with 12 members, 4 outside collaborators and 11 repositories: 9 private (among them client-portal and billing-tools) and 2 public (field-notes and brand-assets).
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Billing and plans page; organization People and Repositories pages

entries.body: The organization has two owners, Dana Whitcomb (managing partner) and Theo Marsh (operations lead). No other member or collaborator holds the owner role.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization People page, filtered to the Owner role

entries.body: Two-factor authentication is not required for the organization: the requirement setting is off. The People page shows 3 of 12 members and 2 of 4 outside collaborators without two-factor authentication enabled. No billing manager is assigned.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Authentication security page; People page, two-factor authentication filter

entries.body: Dana Whitcomb's account uses a passkey for two-factor authentication; no SMS method is registered.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: The owner's own account security page, viewed with the owner on the engagement date

entries.body: Theo Marsh reports using a TOTP authenticator app for two-factor authentication. Which methods are registered on the account (any passkey, security key or SMS fallback) was not seen.
entries.label: UNKNOWN
entries.source: Interview with the owner on the engagement date; the owner's account security page was not viewed

entries.body: SAML single sign-on is not available on the current plan and is not configured. IP allow lists and restricted email notifications are likewise not offered: all three require GitHub Enterprise Cloud, and the organization is on the Team plan.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Authentication security page; Billing and plans page

entries.body: Base permissions for organization members are set to Write: every member can push to every organization repository.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Member privileges page

entries.body: Member privileges: members can create both public and private repositories. Pages creation is disallowed for members and no repository has a published Pages site. Forking of private repositories is not allowed (the default).
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Member privileges page; each public repository's Pages settings

entries.body: Four outside collaborators. One is a staff member of a former IT vendor: write access to client-portal, no two-factor authentication, last activity in the repository in March 2026, when the vendor engagement ended. Repository administrators may invite outside collaborators (the default; the owner-only restriction requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud). No collaborator access review is on record.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization People page, Outside collaborators tab; client-portal Collaborators and teams page and commit history

entries.body: OAuth app access restrictions are not set up. App access requests are enabled for members and outside collaborators, and repository administrators may install GitHub Apps for their repositories (the default). Three GitHub Apps are installed: a CI service and a dependency-update service, both owned by Theo Marsh, and a chat notification app installed by a former staff member, with no internal owner on record.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, OAuth app policy, GitHub Apps and Member privileges pages

entries.body: Personal access token policy: fine-grained tokens can access the organization without approval, and classic tokens are allowed. Three fine-grained tokens are listed with access; one was last used in May 2026.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Personal access tokens pages (settings, active tokens)

entries.body: Two classic personal access tokens are known to have been created for organization work: one by Theo Marsh for the billing-tools deploy script, and one by the former vendor's staff member. Whether either still reaches the organization is not known: without SAML single sign-on, classic tokens are not listed on the organization's token pages.
entries.label: UNKNOWN
entries.source: Interview with the owners; billing-tools deploy script configuration (token name only)

entries.body: Whether anyone still uses the chat notification app or the CI service installation, and who would own the chat app, is not known.
entries.label: UNKNOWN
entries.source: Interview with the owners; the apps' configuration pages show repository access but not use

entries.body: Two deploy keys exist, both on client-portal: one read-write, one read-only. Neither has an owner or review date recorded. The organization-level deploy key policy is not offered on the Team plan.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: client-portal Deploy keys settings page; organization Member privileges page

entries.body: Actions policy: all actions and reusable workflows are allowed. Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions: read and write. Fork pull request workflows require approval for first-time contributors only. Artifact and log retention: 90 days (the default). No self-hosted runners are registered, and repository-level self-hosted runners are allowed for all repositories.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Actions General page and Runners page

entries.body: Six organization Actions secrets. Two (a deployment credential and a notification endpoint) are available to all repositories, public ones included; four are scoped to selected repositories. No accepted-exposure record exists for the two shared secrets.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Secrets and variables, Actions page (names and repository access only)

entries.body: field-notes (public) carries a workflow triggered on pull_request_target that checks out the pull request's head and runs its build script.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: field-notes workflow files, read on the default branch

entries.body: Security defaults for new repositories: secret scanning on for public repositories only, push protection off, Dependabot alerts on, Dependabot security updates off. No organization ruleset exists. Private vulnerability reporting is not enabled on either public repository.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Advanced Security configurations and Rulesets pages; each public repository's Security settings

entries.body: Three organization webhooks. One delivers to the chat notification service, with a secret set and SSL verification on; its deliveries succeed. One delivers to an internal intake endpoint for billing-tools with no secret set (SSL verification on); its deliveries succeed. Both are owned by Theo Marsh. One delivers to ci-old.aldercreek.example, with a secret set: its deliveries failed from April 2026 and have returned success responses again since October 2026.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Webhooks page and each webhook's Recent deliveries tab

entries.body: The firm decommissioned the ci-old server in April 2026; its DNS name was never removed.
entries.label: ON RECORD
entries.source: The owners' account of the server's retirement

entries.body: Who operates the endpoint at ci-old.aldercreek.example now, and so who has been receiving the organization's webhook payloads since October 2026, is not known.
entries.label: UNKNOWN
entries.source: Follows from F1 and F2; not yet investigated

entries.body: Audit log settings: IP addresses are not displayed. No export of the audit log has been taken. Identifying token-performed events requires GitHub Enterprise Cloud.
entries.label: VERIFIED
entries.source: Organization settings, Audit log page

entries.body: Both owners state the audit log has not been reviewed since the organization was created.
entries.label: ON RECORD
entries.source: Interview with the owners

entries.body: The linked Microsoft 365 tenant: both owners sign in to GitHub with the same identities as the tenant (accounts registered to their tenant mailboxes), and both hold highly privileged roles there. The firm's own Microsoft 365 review records phishing-resistant MFA as not yet enforced for the highly privileged roles (MS.AAD.3.6v1, Gap in that review).
entries.label: ON RECORD
entries.source: The firm's own Microsoft 365 review, as provided by the firm; not re-tested in this engagement
